privacy.lead: How SAVIS Group collects, uses and protects personal data on this website.
s: Who we are
This website is operated by SAVIS Group (SAVIS Technology Joint Stock Company), headquartered in Hanoi, VietNam. For privacy questions contact info@savis-group.com.
Data we collect

Information you give us through our forms: the contact form (name, organisation, work email, country, phone and message) and the report and whitepaper download forms (first and last name, business email, company, job title, phone, country, the title you requested and your consent choices); technical data such as IP address, browser and pages visited; and cookie data as described in our Cookie Policy.
Why we use it

To answer enquiries and provide information you request, including sending the report or whitepaper you download and following up on that request; with your separate opt-in, to send you news, research and event invitations; to operate, secure and improve the website; and, with your consent, to measure website use. We do not sell personal data.
Legal basis

Your consent, our legitimate interest in responding to business enquiries and securing the site, and compliance with legal obligations — under VietNam's personal data protection law and, where applicable, the EU GDPR and other local laws.
Sharing

With SAVIS Group companies and offices that handle your enquiry, and with service providers bound by contract, including HubSpot (our CRM and form service, which receives the data you submit in our forms), hosting, email and analytics providers. Transfers outside your country are protected by appropriate safeguards.
Retention

Enquiry data is kept for as long as needed to handle the enquiry and our business relationship, then deleted or anonymised. You can unsubscribe from follow-up emails at any time through the link in each email or by contacting info@savis-group.com.
Your rights

Depending on your location, you may request access, correction, deletion, restriction or portability of your data, withdraw consent and object to processing. Contact info@savis-group.com. You may also complain to your data protection authority.
Security
We apply technical and organisational measures aligned with ISO/IEC 27001.
Changes
We may update this policy; the date below shows the latest version.

cookies.lead: Which cookies this website uses and how you can control them.
s: What cookies are
Cookies and similar technologies are small files stored on your device that help a website work and understand how it is used.
Strictly necessary
Required for the website to work and to remember your cookie choice. These are always on.
Analytics
Help us understand how visitors use the website so we can improve it. Used only if you accept analytics cookies.
Marketing
Used to measure campaigns and show relevant content on other platforms. Used only if you accept marketing cookies.
Your choices
You can accept all, reject non-essential cookies, or choose by category. Change your choice at any time with the “Cookie settings” link in the footer, or through your browser settings.

steps: Citizens enrol at centres or on mobile.
Data flows to enrolment, ABIS and issuance.
Credentials are signed by the national PKI.
Public services authenticate and verify citizens.
Citizens hold credentials in the wallet.
They present via OpenID4VP or ISO 18013-5.
Issuer signatures are checked against Trusted Lists.
Banks, telcos and agencies accept the credential.
Users sign in without a password.
The authenticator answers a FIDO2 challenge.
Keys are verified; policy is enforced.
Applications receive a signed assertion.
Customers transact on any channel.
Channels call SAM Auth Server.
Keys and evidence are protected in hardware.
Core banking, ACS and SOC receive verified results.
The user taps or inserts TrustPass.
The channel relays the challenge.
The key signs inside the secure element.
The bank verifies before executing.
The signer approves on the phone.
Apps call the CSC API.
Keys sign inside the remote QSCD.
Signed documents are timestamped and archived.
Traffic leaves sites and data centres.
It enters the gateway.
Keys are exchanged with hybrid PQC.
Applications and partners receive protected traffic.
Applications request trust services.
Calls arrive by API.
Keys stay inside the appliance's HSM.
Results return to bank and government systems.
